title: The Morrison Terrace and early Black bands in the Loop
summary: They discuss Wickliffe at the Morrison Terrace, claimed as the first Black jazz band in the Loop, and earlier Loop bands such as Elgar's.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Schauffner speaks about being with Wickliffe and mentioned a place called Terrace. Now, that's why. When you said Terrace. Oh.

There was another one. The Morrison Terrace. I wasn't with him. That was before I joined him. He had played the Morrison Terrace in the Morrison Hotel. Oh. The Morrison Terrace. And that was the first time a colored jazz band, or in fact any colored band, had been in the loop, I think, to my knowledge.
Well, no.
That was before 1920. Algar had been in the loop?
In 1918, yeah. With a band that was playing when dancing became very popular. Yes. They had bands in every hotel.
Yes.
Oh, yes. Might have been with the, well, earlier he was in the loop with the Byron Brothers. At a restaurant.
Yes, Byron Brothers, yeah. At a restaurant.
And right after that, he went into a hotel.
Yes.
Maybe the Blackstone or something.
Stratford, I imagine it was. Maybe the Stratford.
I think so. You're right. Stratford. And they were there for months. Mm-hmm. Eight months, ten months. So that was one of the earliest.
Mm-hmm. Yes, I'd forgotten that. You're right.
Then, of course, several others got into the loop. Wade.
Yes, Jimmy Wade, yes. He played the loop.
And I think Sammy Stewart for a while.
Yes. Mm-hmm.
And then, of course, it became a frequent. But you may have played one of the earliest cabaret jobs. Or Wycliffe, I mean, may have played one of the very earliest.
Yes, I think he was the first cabaret job. His was the first cabaret job.
